channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Lucky Star Issue 5: Camera-Less
item.description: Fifth issue of San Francisco indie photography magazine dedicated to camera-less and alternative photographic processes. Exploring experimental, often abstract methods including pinhole, lumen, cyanotype, chemigram, photogram, chlorophyll printing and more. Artists challenged to put down the camera and consider the physicality of making an image. Cohesive bodies or series of work encouraged and prioritised. Files must be at least 300 DPI, ready-to-print. Magazine printed at 6×9 inches with potential 9×12 inch full spreads. Artists whose work is accepted contacted via email within a week after deadline. Submissions from artists featured in previous issues considered last. — Deadline: April 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 2026 Booooooom Art & Photo Book Award
item.description: Annual award selecting 6 book projects and 2 zine projects for fully funded publication in partnership with Bookmobile. Books up to 100 pages and 10×10 inches, printed in 100 copies. Zines up to 36 pages, 5×7 inches, printed in 25 copies. Open to all artists, illustrators, and photographers. Non-members may submit one free zine proposal or pay $20 for a book proposal. Members submit unlimited at no extra cost. — Deadline: June 5, 2026. Fee: Free (zines) / $20 (books). Prize: Publication (6 books + 2 zines printed).

item.title: Nachleben 2026 · Grenze-Arsenali Fotografici
item.description: Open call for the Nachleben photography festival in Verona, Italy, September 2026. Three photographers or collectives selected for exhibition. Selected artists receive two nights accommodation during opening weekend, meals, travel reimbursement up to €300, and a production budget of up to €1,000 for prints and installation. Open to photographers of any age. No thematic restrictions — jury selects on artistic merit. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: €28. Prize: Exhibition + €300 travel + €1,000 print budget.

item.title: NOVA24 2026 Project Open Call
item.description: Third edition of an indie photo and film festival in Detroit. Open call for photographers and filmmakers to present experimental and innovative work. Selected projects exhibited during the festival across indoor and outdoor projection galleries, mural installations, gallery exhibitions, film screenings, and artist talks. Festival runs June 26 – July 31, 2026 across multiple Detroit venues. Founded in 2023 to connect Detroit's lens-based creative community with international audiences. — Deadline: April 22, 2026. Fee: $10 donation (free for limited income). Prize: Exhibition at festival.

item.title: Archifoto 2026 — Architecture & Landscape · La Chambre
item.description: Eighth edition of the European architectural photography competition organised by La Chambre and Maison Européenne de l'Architecture – Rhin supérieur. Theme: Architecture & Landscape — photographs revealing complementarities or tensions between architecture and landscape, exploring how they shape territories and communities amid climate and demographic changes. Five nominees each receive €500 and are exhibited at La Chambre in Strasbourg in autumn 2026, with touring exhibitions across partner venues in the Upper Rhine region. Running since 2010, combining documentary and artistic perspectives on current architectural issues. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: €500 + exhibition.

item.title: Appalachian Nature Art & Photography Competition & Exhibition · Arcadian Gallery
item.description: Regional competition celebrating the beauty of nature across the Appalachian region. Photography-specific awards include Best of Show Photography ($500), Best Landscape Photography ($250), and Best Living Thing Photography ($250), plus a People's Choice Award ($250). Two-dimensional artwork or photography depicting Appalachian nature — landscapes, plants, wildlife, and other natural subjects from any Appalachian state. Exhibition May 15 – June 20, 2026 at Arcadian Gallery in Cumberland, MD. Juried by Steven David Johnson (photography) and Terry Miller (art). — Deadline: April 7, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $500 Best of Show + additional awards.

item.title: Athens Photo Festival Dummy Award 2026
item.description: International photobook dummy competition run by the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photographers and artists who use photography, regardless of age or nationality. Winner receives a publishing contract with Chose Commune for the production of a photobook with a production budget of up to €15,000 and a minimum print run of 400 copies. Winning project included in the festival's main exhibition programme at Benaki Museum in Athens. Twenty shortlisted dummies exhibited at the festival, ten included in the printed catalogue. Submit digitally via online form (PDF, max 10 MB) and mail one physical dummy copy postmarked by the deadline. Projects should be finalized upon submission. If already printed, editions must be under 100 copies. Fee €25 per project, €15 for additional projects by the same applicant. — Deadline: April 28, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Photobook contract (up to €15,000) + exhibition.

item.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2026
item.description: First edition of a new international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2026. Fourteen winners honoured at an awards ceremony in Tours in early May. Categories: Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography, each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award. Winners receive the ABSURIA Trophy — a physical gold statuette created specifically for the contest. All nominees exhibited in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Printing costs covered by organisers. AI-generated images not accepted. Fee varies by number of works submitted: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 images per registration. — Deadline: April 26, 2026. Fee: €20–€50. Prize: Exhibition + trophy.

item.title: Motion · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring motion in still images. Photography cannot create the illusion of motion the way moving images can, yet photographers have developed powerful techniques for capturing and evoking it — from long exposures and motion blur to freezing split-second moments of action. PH21 Gallery invites submissions for a themed group show at their venue in Barcelona's historic Gothic Quarter. One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions will be announced. Curator's choice receives free entry (up to 15 images) for the next PH21 exhibition. Early bird deadline April 20 at reduced rates; final deadline April 27. Special rate for students and unwaged (€15–€20). All photographers 18+ worldwide may enter with original work. Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1200px. Exhibition June 27 – July 21, 2026. — Deadline: April 27, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Manipulation & Illusion · Co-Ex Collaborative
item.description: Open call exploring the terrain between what is seen and what is constructed. Seeking work that engages with manipulation and illusion as they relate to perception, belief, identity, and power. Themes include optical, sensory, and spatial illusion; distortion, misdirection, and scale; unreliable memory; propaganda and political persuasion; digital manipulation and curated environments; institutional narratives and manufactured truth; manipulation as artistic method; and altered materials, images, and data. All disciplines welcome — photography, visual art, design, and fine craft. Submissions accepted exclusively through the Co-Ex Collaborative website portal. Selected work featured in a curated online collection. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Epson International Pano Awards 2026
item.description: 17th edition of the world's largest international competition for panoramic photography. Three main categories: Open (professional and amateur, $22/image), Amateur (non-professional photographers earning less than $20,000 from photography, $20/image), and VR/360 ($20/image) — plus a new Aerial category for drone and aircraft images. Total prize pool over US$50,000 including $15,000 in cash prizes. Open category winner receives a package exceeding $11,000. Early-bird entries close June 22 at standard rates; late entries accepted through July 13 at higher rates. Photographers who enter during the early-bird period are eligible for the $1,000 Curator's Award. Images must be panoramic format with aspect ratio greater than 2:1 (or less than 1:2 for verticals). All photographic capture methods welcome including digital, film, and stitched panoramas. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 13, 2026. Fee: $20–$22. Prize: US$50,000+ total prize pool.

item.title: REMEDY Photo Festival — Open Call 2026
item.description: Photography festival focused on health, care, lived experience, and representation. Seeking photographic work exploring health in its broadest sense — physical, mental, chronic, invisible, communal, or systemic. Welcomes personal stories, portraiture, documentary, photojournalism, and fine art photography. Particularly interested in work by photographers with lived experience of long-term health conditions. Selected artists included in curated group exhibition at a photography gallery in Lincoln, with additional venues across Lincolnshire. No entry fee and no cost to exhibit — printing and display costs covered by the festival. Exhibition June 1–30, 2026. Past featured photographers include Anthony Luvera and JA Mortram. — Deadline: April 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SQUARE Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Challenging photographers to compose within the square format — the most iconic and persistent format in photography. All photographic genres welcome including portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, and conceptual work. Twelve images selected for three-month exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 14×14 framing, and custom matting. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1 – October 31, 2026. — Deadline: June 13, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Cumberland Valley Photographers 2026 · Washington County Museum of Fine Arts
item.description: Annual juried photography exhibition at the Washington County Museum of Fine Arts, this year celebrating contemporary perspectives as the nation approaches its 250th anniversary. Photographers explore history, identity, place, and civic life through four themes: Unfinished Revolutions, Power of Place, Tell Everyone's Story, and American Experiment. Respond literally or metaphorically through documentary, conceptual, figurative, or abstract approaches. All photographic processes accepted. Submissions open April 1–30, 2026. Selected work exhibited June 20 – October 11, 2026. Open to photographers from Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Washington, DC. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Issue 02: Eerie
item.description: Second issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. Issue 02, guest curated by Karla Guerrero (Mexico City-based photographer, curator, and editor active in the contemporary photography scene), explores the theme Eerie — quiet disturbance, a poetics of phantasmagoria where images silently evoke meaning. The eerie as the fleeting suggestion that something unnameable lingers just beneath what we think we see. Something quietly disturbing. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px) with artist statement and bio. Upload work to Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files: Name_Series_Title_01. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers. — Deadline: April 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Canon Female Photojournalist Grant 2026 · Visa pour l'Image
item.description: 26th edition of the grant awarded in partnership with Canon, supporting female photojournalists pursuing long-term documentary projects. Winner receives €8,000 to support completion of an existing project or facilitate the making of a new one. Winning project exhibited at the Visa pour l'Image festival in Perpignan, France, September 2026. Open to professional female photojournalists worldwide, no age or nationality restrictions. Free entry. Winner selected in June by a jury of industry experts. Application window: March 18 – May 19, 2026. — Deadline: May 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000.

item.title: A Black Perspective: Celebrating the Voice & Vision · PhotoSC
item.description: Exhibition celebrating diverse narratives by Black photographers exploring resilience, heritage, joy, identity, and extraordinary aspects of Black life. Various photographic styles welcome including alternative practices and collage work. Juried by Arnika Dawkins, fine art photographer and founder of the Arnika Dawkins Gallery in Atlanta, specializing in imagery by and of African Americans. Selected work exhibited May 21 – June 19, 2026 at PhotoSC gallery, 918 Lady Street, Columbia, SC. Work must be printed 8x10" to 16x20", framed, and ready to hang. — Deadline: April 18, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ANIMAL LIFE · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition celebrating the complexity and individuality of animals. Photographers invited to explore animal subjects with curiosity, empathy, and imagination — companion animals, wildlife, insects, and sea life through observation, environmental portraiture, documentary, or experimental approaches. Welcomes diverse perspectives on human-animal relationships. All lens-based photographic and lens-based art practices welcome, including black and white, color, traditional and non-traditional processes. Images showcasing violence or inhumane treatment will not be considered. — Deadline: April 19, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: FFSP 2026 — Italian Photographers Open Call · Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo
item.description: Open call for Italian photographers as part of the São Paulo Photography Festival 2026, organized by the Italian Cultural Institute of São Paulo. Fifteen photographers will be selected for a free exhibition in May 2026 as part of the festival's official programme. One finalist will receive a round-trip flight between Brazil and Italy and official participation in FFSP 2026, fostering cultural and professional exchange between the two countries. Open to Italian citizens of legal age residing in Brazil or Italy. Submit 1 to 5 photographs on any theme of your choice. — Deadline: April 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Womanhood · Photobook Cafe & Rapid Eye Darkroom
item.description: Sixth quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms exploring the theme of Womanhood with guest judge Francesca Allen. Open to anyone engaging with or experiencing Womanhood in all its forms. 35 selected photographers featured in group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe in London. Three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition with printing by Rapid Eye Darkrooms and curation by Francesca Allen. — Deadline: April 20, 2026. Fee: £25. Prize: Exhibition + zine publication.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Latin America & Caribbean Residency 2026
item.description: Twelve-week fully funded residency at the Delfina Foundation in London, supported by Jorge M. Pérez and El Espacio 23. Open to visual artists based in Latin America, the Caribbean, and related diasporic communities in the United States. Artists from Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, and Argentina are not eligible for this cycle (these countries received dedicated residencies in prior years). Two artists will be selected from this call: one for the autumn 2026 residency (September 21 – December 13) and one for the winter 2027 residency (January 5 – March 25). Apply via Cognito Forms with completed application form — read the Guidance Notes document before applying. — Deadline: April 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fully funded 12-week residency.

item.title: MACK — Debut Photography Book Submissions
item.description: MACK's annual submission window for first-time photobook authors. Founded by Michael Mack (former Managing Director of Steidl) in 2010, MACK is one of the most prestigious art and photography publishers in the world, releasing approximately 40 books per year with artists including Robert Adams, Alec Soth, and Wolfgang Tillmans. This window is specifically for artists who have not previously had a book published — seeking emerging voices and experimental approaches to the book form. Submit a PDF draft sequence and completed submissions form via email during the May 1–31 window only. No WeTransfer, Dropbox, or download links accepted. Email subject line: 'Submission: Debut Photography Book'. Response within one month after the window closes. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: MACK — Photography Submissions
item.description: MACK's annual photography submission window. One of the world's most prestigious art and photography publishers, founded by Michael Mack in 2010 and based in London. This window seeks photobook projects that expand visual vocabulary and challenge expectations of photography's potential, with a special interest in voices and perspectives that are often underrepresented in the photobook landscape. Submit a PDF draft sequence and completed submissions form via email during the June 1–30 window only. No WeTransfer, Dropbox, or download links accepted. Email subject line: 'Submission: Photography'. Response within one month after the window closes. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Graz Residency for International Photographers (GRIP) 2026 · Camera Austria
item.description: One-month residency for early-career photographers and lens-based artists in Graz, Austria. Fifth edition of GRIP, a joint initiative by Camera Austria and Kulturvermittlung Steiermark. Resident works on an ongoing project or develops new work, with access to Camera Austria's 11,000+ volume study library. Residency concludes with a presentation in Camera Austria's exhibition and library space. Open to international early-career artists working with photography and/or lens-based arts. Apply by email with informal statement of purpose and PDF portfolio. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,000 stipend.

item.title: Hidden Narratives Residency 2026 · Photoworks
item.description: Year-long residency engaging with the Royal Geographical Society's historic photographic collection of over one million pieces spanning 1845–1945. Artists explore materials relating to environment and humanitarian themes, developing work examining hidden narratives, loss, and human impact. Includes three research and presentation visits to the UK, a talk at Summit Photo 2026 (July 17–19), and an exhibition at Summit Photo 2027. In partnership with the Royal Geographical Society and the Italian Cultural Institute in London. Open to Italian visual artists, photographers, or practitioners with archive research experience, aged 18+, proficient in English. — Deadline: April 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,500 stipend.

item.title: Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award 2026 · FotoDocument
item.description: Annual £4,000 grant for professional female photographers working on documentary photo essays that address social, environmental, economic, or cultural issues. Landmark 10th edition, supported by Nikon. Selected work must showcase positive solutions and demonstrate practical engagement with the subject matter. Named after Marilyn Stafford, pioneering documentary photographer. Winner's work exhibited at POST, Brighton & Hove's centre for photography, September 17–20, 2026, and featured on Lenscratch and FotoDocument. Open to female photographers (or those identifying as female) aged 18+ at any career stage, any nationality worldwide. Must have completed at least one prior documentary photo essay and already started the proposed project. — Deadline: May 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £4,000.

item.title: Inge Morath Award 2026 · Magnum Foundation
item.description: Annual award supporting women and nonbinary photographers under 30 working on long-term documentary projects. Administered by the Magnum Foundation in cooperation with Magnum Photos and the Inge Morath Estate. The recipient receives $7,500 and one finalist receives $1,000 to support completion of their project. Selected by the full membership of Magnum Photos during their Annual General Meeting, alongside the Inge Morath Estate and the Executive Director of the Magnum Foundation. Named after Austrian-born Magnum photographer Inge Morath (1923–2002). Now in its 25th year. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $7,500 + $1,000 finalist grant.

item.title: Women in Nature — Artist's Commission · Photo Museum Ireland
item.description: Photographic commission by Tóchar Midlands Wetland Restoration and Photo Museum Ireland highlighting the work of women in nature restoration in Ireland. €15,000 commission (including €3,000 travel bursary) for a single artist to create a series of 12 portraits of women in nature, together with photographs of the habitat they are working to restore. Outputs include exhibitions, community conversations, and a publication. Open to artists resident on the island of Ireland working in photography or lens-based media. Judged on creativity and originality (25%), technical skill and execution (20%), impact and storytelling (15%), and track record (10%). Co-financed by the EU Just Transition Fund and the Government of Ireland. — Deadline: April 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €15,000 commission + exhibition + publication.

item.title: Nikon Comedy Wildlife Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Annual international competition celebrating the funniest moments in wildlife photography. Founded in 2015 by Paul Joynson-Hicks and Tom Sullam. Free to enter, open to everyone worldwide with any camera brand. Nine categories: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles/Amphibians/Insects, Fish & Aquatic Species, Nikon Young Photographer, Nikon Junior, Portfolio, Nikon Video, and People's Choice Award. Grand prize: week-long safari for two at Alex Walker's Serian in the Maasai Mara, Kenya. Category winners receive Nikon cameras and lenses plus handmade trophies. Over 10,000 entries from 100+ countries. Proceeds support wildlife conservation. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Kenya safari for 2 + Nikon gear + trophies.

item.title: FLORA — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
item.description: Open call for a printed photobook celebrating the diversity, resilience, subtleties, and poetry of growing things. Images should capture vegetation from mosses and ferns to forests, blossoms, vines, and roots — revealing the nuance of growth, patterns of nature's processes, and the quiet power of plant life in all environments. Selected images featured in a printed FLORA photobook, available through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum donation. Free submissions available for photographers with limited income (email request required before entry). AI use must be disclosed. — Deadline: June 11, 2026. Fee: £15+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: 43rd Center Annual · Houston Center for Photography
item.description: Houston Center for Photography's annual group exhibition, now in its 43rd year. Seeks to highlight current themes, technologies, and practices in photography. Features diverse works from HCP members worldwide — emerging, mid-career, and established photographers. Two artists selected for $500 HCP Juried Membership Honoraria. This year juried by Asha Iman Veal, curator for globally collaborative exhibitions of contemporary art. Exhibition runs June 4 – August 16, 2026. — Deadline: April 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Two $500 honoraria + exhibition.

item.title: Golden Turtle International Wildlife Festival 2026
item.description: International wildlife photography competition in 12 categories: Animals in the Environment, Portrait of the Animal, Animal Behaviour, Microcosm, Underwater World, Art and Nature's Image, Landscape, Magic of Plants, Humans and Nature, Reserved Russia, Mobile Photography, and Youth (two age groups). Up to 20 photos per author. Professional jury of international wildlife photographers. Finalists exhibited in Moscow autumn 2026, published in festival album. No zoo photography except Humans and Nature category. No composites or montage. RAW files required from semifinalists. — Deadline: April 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 150,000 RUB.

item.title: Hasselblad Foundation Nature Photography Grant 2026
item.description: Grant for photographic explorations of nature, landscape, and environment. Emphasis on originality, environmental issues, biodiversity, and human impact on nature and climate. Open to citizens of Nordic countries or permanent residents of the Nordic region. Projects should have a 1–3 year timeframe. — Deadline: May 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 100,000 SEK grant.

item.title: Guest Room: Shana Lopes & Aspen Mays · Der Greif
item.description: Open call curated by Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA) and Aspen Mays (Associate Professor/Chair of Photography, California College of the Arts) exploring the theme "A Little Bit of Magic" — inviting work that engages with doubling, substitution, sleight of hand, constructed realities, staged impossibilities, and illusion in photography. Open to everyone. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with feedback session from the curators. — Deadline: April 2, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: €250 scholarship.

item.title: Photobook Feature — In Focus · Der Greif
item.description: Open call for photobooks to be featured in Der Greif's Articles section with a dedicated editorial write-up. No fixed theme. Seeks photobooks demonstrating strong conceptual thinking, thoughtful sequencing, and an engaged relationship to the medium of the book. Accepts self-published photobooks, artist books, zines, experimental publications, and small-edition press titles. Both recent releases and unpublished or in-progress projects eligible (if publication-ready). — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Jugend fotografiert Deutschland 2025 · laif foundation
item.description: German youth photography contest for ages 10–18, now in its 2025/26 edition. Theme: "Be you. Be seen. Be heard." Submit documentary photo stories on any personally relevant topic. Smartphones or cameras welcome, no prior experience required. Individuals or teams of up to 10 participants with optional coaches from schools, youth centers, or community organizations. Must be residents of Germany. — Deadline: April 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €200–€500 + exhibition.

item.title: RESTART2026 · Lithuanian Photographers' Association
item.description: International photography competition and exhibition for photographers starting their careers or reconsidering their creative direction with new work. Submit a series of 10–20 photographs created after 2021 that has not been fully exhibited or published. 10 finalists exhibit at Prospekto gallery in Vilnius. Top 3 winners receive individual exhibitions at Vilnius Photography Gallery the following year with partial production support. Printed catalogue for finalists. Featured on photography.lt and screened at NIDA Meeting Photography symposium in September. — Deadline: April 12, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: Solo exhibition + catalogue.

item.title: DPPF 2026 Sports Photography Grants
item.description: Grants supporting emerging and early-career sports photographers with fewer than 3 years cumulative paid professional sports photography experience. Seven photographers receive $5,000 each for career development plus expenses-paid trip to the Sports Photography Gathering (September 16–18, 2026). Up to 3 winners eligible for year-long mentorship with Advisory Board members. Up to 3 additional applicants receive $2,500 Development Grants. Open worldwide except countries under active US sanctions. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 7 × $5,000 + 3 × $2,500.

item.title: Bowness Photography Prize 2026
item.description: Australia's richest photography prize, now in its 20th year. Open to Australian citizens or permanent residents (12+ months). Winner receives $50,000 AUD and acquisition into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. Wai Tang Commissioning Award of $10,000 for a future exhibition. People's Choice Award of $5,000. Finalists exhibited at MAPh gallery. Accepts still photo-based media including analogue and digital photography produced within the past year. Up to 3 works per $55 entry. AI permitted only if not the substantial or overriding input. Entries open April 16, 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $55 AUD. Prize: $50,000 + $10,000 + $5,000 + 2 × $2,500.

item.title: Home · Photography 4 Humanity
item.description: Global open call exploring the theme of home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. In partnership with Fotografiska Emerging and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. Selected works will be exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Curated by James Nachtwey and Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska Global VP Artistic Direction). Open to emerging photographers worldwide. 31 artists selected: 1 main image, 10 runner-ups, 20 honorable mentions. All forms of lens-based photography welcome, analog or digital. AI-generated or prompt-based images not accepted. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exibart Street Photography Contest — 5th Edition
item.description: Fifth edition of the international street photography contest by Exibart Street, Italy's leading contemporary art magazine. Two categories: Best Single Photo (€10) and Best Series of 3–9 images (€49). Winners receive a Leica Q3 or Xiaomi 17 Ultra with Leica lenses, plus interviews and editorial coverage across the Exibart network. Sponsored by Leica Camera. Open to photographers worldwide. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €10–€49. Prize: Leica Q3 + Xiaomi 17 Ultra + publication.

item.title: Flanelle Print No. 47 — July 2026
item.description: Montreal-based fashion and arts magazine (est. 2012) accepting submissions for Print No. 47, publishing July 2026. Open to artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Selected work featured in quarterly print and digital magazine with international distribution. Two-phase review process. Work must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle. Paid upgrade options available for cover placement and priority publishing. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Embracing Our Differences 2027 Outdoor Exhibition
item.description: International outdoor juried exhibition in its 23rd year. 50 selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels (16 ft × 12.5 ft) in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January to April 2027. Three awards: $2,000 Best-in-Show Adult, $2,000 Best-in-Show Student, $2,000 People's Choice. Work must reflect themes of diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect. Accepts photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art. Horizontal orientation only. No limit on entries per artist. 150-word artist statement required. Over 5.2 million visitors since 2004. AI-generated work not accepted. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000.

item.title: Ephemere Photo Journal Vol. 2 — Triplicities
item.description: Submit text-driven photo features exploring "Triplicities: The Magic of Three" — Time's Arrow, The Life Cycle, The Dialectic. Accepted formats include personal essays, critical essays, photo-poetry, philosophical explorations, interviews, and reviews. Published in a collectible large-format newsprint journal printed in Japan. Shortlisted authors work directly with editors in a collaborative editing process. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: ¥10,000 + publication.

item.title: European Landscapes Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call for photographs of European landscapes — lakes, rivers, sea, trees, sunsets, storms, gardens. Selected work published in a printed photo book. No collage, manipulated, or AI-generated photos accepted. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Northern Europe Landscapes Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call for photographs of northern European natural and rural landscapes (no buildings). Selected work published in a printed photo book. No collage, manipulated, or AI-generated photos accepted. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Fresh Legs 2026 · Galleri Heike Arndt DK
item.description: Annual group exhibition initiative running since 2013, presenting painting, sculpture, illustration, drawing, street art, photography, short film, animation, and related media. Exhibition at two Berlin venues: Galleri Heike Arndt DK (June–October 2026) and INSELGALERIE Berlin (June–July 2026). No submission fee; €40 exhibition fee if accepted. Selected works must remain available for 12 months for potential follow-up exhibitions. All works must be for sale. Gallery takes 30–50% commission on sales. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: I Can Buy Myself Flowers · Haze Gallery
item.description: HAZEGALLERY, the curatorial platform of PURPLEHAZE Magazine, invites artists and image-makers to participate in a curated pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam alongside the launch of PURPLEHAZE Print Issue 012. Theme explores autonomy as identity, rituals of independence, intimacy turned inward, beauty chosen rather than granted, solitude as clarity, and desire as self-directed. Accepts fashion, fine art, and documentary photography, works on paper, fine art prints, and short looping video works. Selected artists participate in the June 2026 Amsterdam exhibition and may be published in the print issue. — Deadline: April 16, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Les Mots du Phare Vol. 04: Futur(s) · Linea Recta Books
item.description: Open call for black-and-white photography for Vol. 04 of Les Mots du Phare, a print publication by Linea Recta Books and Le Phare Collectif. Theme: Futur(s) — imagining what seems impossible, a tomorrow, an after, a continuation. Not the end of the world, but the courage to imagine what is possible. Selected images will be featured in the printed edition alongside text contributions from members of the collective. Submit up to 4 B&W photos combined into one PDF via email. — Deadline: April 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Night Aesthetics · Fotografiska
item.description: Open call exploring the visual world of the night. Looking for works that engage with light, movement, atmosphere, intimacy, and the energy that appears when the day lets go. Whether captured on a crowded dance floor, in a quiet street, or somewhere in between. Welcomes lens-based photography in all forms including analog and digital. Three winners each receive €2,500 and feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform. In partnership with Jägermeister. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3 × €2,500.
